title: Failure-domain containment and progressive failover for Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers have tight latency and isolation SLOs. During region outages, control plane upgrades, or noisy-tenant incidents we currently have two pain points: (1) bulk failover strategies that move all traffic between regions leading to cold KV cache and SLA misses for many tenants, and (2) cross-tenant blast radius during upgrades or overloaded nodes because our control plane and routing decisions are not sufficiently failure-domain aware.

Goal: Implement a failure-domain containment strategy combined with progressive multi-region failover and tenant-scoped circuit breakers and load-shedding so that (a) healthy tenants maintain their SLOs whenever possible, (b) noisy or degraded tenants are degraded gracefully without bringing down the region, and (c) rolling upgrades can be performed with tenant pinning and automated rollback when recovery metrics degrade.

Implementation notes: prefer small control-plane feature flags to reduce blast radius, add api for "pin_tenants_to_version", and ensure KMS/HSM operations remain in control-plane-safe path.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Per-tenant SLO breach rate must be reduced by 60% during simulated partial-region outage compared to today.
2) Rolling upgrade process supports tenant pinning and canary waves with automated rollback on defined regressions.
3) Circuit breaker triggers are tenant-scoped and prevent more than 5% of healthy tenants from experiencing downstream errors during high-noise incidents.
4) New dashboards show tenant-level failover status, circuit breaker triggers, and cache-warmth metrics.
design_notes:
High-level design components:
- Failure-domain tagging: mark infra units (hosts, pods, zones) with failure-domain ids and ensure routing layer uses tags to avoid correlated targets.
- Progressive failover policy: instead of full cutover, implement staged traffic shifting with retention of warm KV caches where possible (prefix-affinity TTLs) and configurable time windows for successive waves.
- Tenant-scoped circuit breakers: per-tenant token bucket and error-rate detector that trips to a degraded policy (rate limit to a lower throughput, degrade model variant, or return 429/503 with retry-after) before global throttles kick in.
- Control plane partitioning: logical isolation for control plane operations (upgrades, config pushes) so tenant groups can be paused or pinned to previous runtime during rollout.
- Upgrade safety: rolling upgrade orchestrator adds a trial traffic mirror step, smoke checks, regression signals (p95 latency, error-rate, token-per-second), and automatic rollback hooks.
- Observability: add tenant-level metrics for cache hit ratio, warm-start fraction, circuit_breaker_state, and per-wave failover progression.
- Routing fallback: prefer same-region warm cache endpoints, then region-local cold endpoints, then cross-region endpoints. Allow per-customer policy overrides.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (dev/stage): implement tenant-scoped circuit breaker and metrics instrumentation behind feature flag. Run chaos tests in stage to validate isolation.
Phase 2 (canary): enable progressive failover in a single region for low-traffic dedicated pools; perform rolling upgrades with tenant pinning for 5% of tenants.
Phase 3 (regional ramp): expand progressive failover across two regions and validate cross-region KV cache rehydration heuristics.
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default for Dedicated and optional opt-in for Private deployments with configuration toggles.

Rollback plan: immediate rollback to previous control-plane version if canary signals show >10% p95 regression or >2x error-rate in pinned tenants. Emergency tenant-isolation API to force pin or drain specific tenant traffic.
test_plan:
Automated tests:
- Unit tests for circuit breaker state machine and routing decision logic.
- Integration tests that simulate a noisy tenant that exceeds quotas and validate neighbors are unaffected.
- End-to-end chaos tests: simulate zone loss, slow network, upgrade-induced latency spikes and verify progressive failover wave timings and cache-warmth metrics.
- Performance tests: measure cold-start token latency and compare against baseline; ensure progressive failover reduces p99 spikes.
- DR drills: run multi-region failover playbook with SREs and record runbook timings and operator actions.
tasks:
- T1: Add failure-domain tags to infra metadata and expose in routing decisions (ENG/Ashwin).
- T2: Implement per-tenant circuit breaker state machine with durable state (Redis or Postgres) and feature flag (ENG/Marcus).
- T3: Build rolling-upgrade orchestrator hooks for tenant pinning and trial mirror traffic (ENG/Sophia).
- T4: Instrument tenant-level metrics and dashboards (ENG/Observability team).
- T5: Create stage chaos scripts and add to CI (ENG/Chaos team).
- T6: Update runbooks and create runbook play for emergency tenant isolation (SRE/Oncall).
- T7: Docs and API surface for ops teams and customer success to request tenant pinning (DX/Docs).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Too-aggressive circuit breaker thresholds may degrade customer experience for borderline tenants. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds, analyze telemetry for two weeks, then tighten.
Risk: Increased control-plane complexity may introduce bugs. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, thorough integration tests, and a safety-proxy that can switch to a fallback policy.
Risk: Cross-region KV rehydration could create burst traffic. Mitigation: backoff and batch rehydration windows with jitter.
Risk: Private/on-prem deployments may have variable topology. Mitigation: expose tuning knobs and validate with 2-3 pilot customers before GA.

metrics:
Primary metrics to track:
- tenant_slo_breach_rate (baseline vs. during incidents)
- number_of_tenants_pin_enabled
- average_cache_warm_fraction_during_failover
- circuit_breaker_trigger_rate_per_tenant
- time_to_roll_back_on_regression
- p95 and p99 latency changes during canary and regional ramps
